content: I am not myself an expert in algebraic number theory, but my colleague Romyar Sharifi kindly pointed me towards his lecture notes where he proves (the Dirichlet density version of) the Chebotarev density theorem in Section 7. Roughly speaking, the idea is to first prove Chebotarev for cyclotomic extensions, then for abelian extensions (which in particular covers the case of cyclic extensions), and then arbitrary extensions. The latter two steps are mostly algebraic number theory in nature; it is just the first step in which analytic methods are used. It seems the cyclotomic case is very similar in spirit to the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions (and indeed generalizes that theorem). I made a preliminary attempt to state some of the key steps in the blueprint at https://github.com/AlexKontorovich/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/pull/222 , focusing on the cyclotomic case. But I am not very confident that this is the optimal route, I'm hoping there is someone who is more familiar with the algebraic number theory side of things who can chime in.

I'm reviving this old thread now that we have the issues system in place. I have in the blueprint a very sketchy route to the Chebotarev density theorem, based on (a) first establishing this theorem for cyclotomic extensions; (b) using this to establish the theorem for abelian extensions, and then (c) doing arbitrary extensions. All three steps are very sketchy right now, pointing to some notes of Sharifi. This is in large part because I do not have the algebraic number theory background to properly flesh out a blueprint for any of these steps. So I have opened PNT#584 as a blueprinting task (not a formalization task) to provide a more detailed blueprint for (a), for instance breaking up the three lemmas 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.3 currently in the blueprint into smaller pieces, that one can then hopefully try to formalize with further issues. This would be a task for someone expert in algebraic number theory but would not require significant expertise with Lean.
Me, @Chris Birkbeck and @Xavier Roblot are thinking about Chebotarev. Is anyone else currently working on it? We are interested in anything has been done in the last year :).

Not much, but I think all the ingredients are there for a direct analytic proof (along the lines for Strong PNT)? We could start with abelian extensions via Hecke characters. That would already be a good milestone, right? And then do Brauer induction. (I assume that's the path you have in mind?) Are you planning to follow something like Lagarias-Odlyzko?

Yeah, right now things are stalled, in large part because we lack an expert in algebraic number theory to decide upon what the best path to take is. You are welcome to run such a project within PNT (using the blueprint and opening it up to volunteers) or you can do things separately (but presumably you will need some PNT machinery unless you just want to do the Dirichlet density version). In any case I'd be happy to talk more about it here.
Well, since we are mainly algebraic number theorists we were thinking to the Dirichlet version. The only drawback we see is that this would not contain an explicit version, but it seems enough to us.

OK, then I guess we could wait on our end to see what you decide is best for the Dirichlet density version and then adapt your framework for a PNT-type result. Are you aiming for a Mathlib-level formalization?

Hi Riccardo, could it be worthwhile to hop on a quick zoom call and discuss approaches? In my mind, the algebraic number theory + L-functions are largely there, so it's a matter of hooking that up to the complex analysis in PNT+...

Ah, right, the answer very much depends on whether you're hoping for Mathlib quality code. But even that might be doable, depending on how quickly we can move on the Residue Theorem (from the ICERM workshop)...
I personally would be much happier if it wasn't the Dirichlet density version, but I believe that is all that would be needed for FLT (which implies existence, not good estimates...)
Which version would you want?

Even just getting the definitions and statement right for the Dirichlet version could be useful for setting up the PNT version. So one compromise is to have Mathlib-level _definitions_ but prototype-level _proofs_, at least initially. (Here I am using the classification in page 16 of my ICERM talk
integrated.pdf on the IEANTN, which I realize that I should share on this zulip.)

The main thing I think is to get the basic properties of Dedekind zeta functions (meromorphic continuation, Euler factorization, residue at s=1, some basic upper bounds). The existing machinery in PNT+ can take it from there.
Functional equation is not needed, though I guess it would be nice eventually

So, our goal is to have some version of Chebotarev in mathlib in a reasonable amount of time. We are convinced the Dirichlet version is doable, but we also agree the other one is mathematically more precise, so in principle it would be better to have that. On the other hand we are less sure it's reasonable to have it in mathlib in the not-so-far future.
If we proved this version, would that give you enough algebraic number theory for you to then take it from there to do this Lagarias-Odlyzko version you want?

It would certainly be a good starting base. There was enough work on Dirichlet L-functions in Mathlib for instance at https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.html to get the PNT in arithmetic progressions relatively easily from our framework. So if you can get the Mathlib support for Dedekind functions some of the way towards its existing support for Dirichlet L-functions then we could probably take it from there.
OK, thanks for the answer! @Alex Kontorovich if you want we may have a zoom call when we have a more precise plan, we are still thinking about the mathematical strategy.

It seems an autoformalization project to formalize the sum-product counterexample also needed some facts about Dedekind zeta functions that were not yet in Mathlib: #Autoformalization > Discussion: the sum-product counterexample . Perhaps this can inform what shape of results about such functions one should target for Mathlib.
Yes,, they formalised meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Dedekind zeta and this wasn't completely autonomous, this was where the most human guidance was needed.

So @Xavier Roblot , @Riccardo Brasca and I now have a sorry-free proof of the Dirichlet version of Chebotarev's density theorem. You can find it here. We also unformalised the results into a blueprint which makes it easier to explore. We still need to clean up the results a lot more before they are at mathlib level, but maybe you can look at what is here and see if you can use if to prove the more explicit versions?

Just to note we ran comparator and it all came back fine. Also there is a formalisation.yaml if you are interested, but the tl;dr is: About 10 days on a Claude max subscription, with some maths guidance from ChatGPT pro and some initial reviews from us to check the statements were correct.
